incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'acme-enterprise-pool-1' GPU utilization 98% (sustained). Queue latency > 2s. Single tenant 'acme-enterprise' observed using ~92% of allocatable GPUs. Paging @oncall-sre. Incident severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-pool-exhaustion

oncall-sre: Oncall here, joining. Adding context channel and pulling metrics. @ben-ing-runtime can you post the pool state and autoscaler logs? :eyes:

ben-eng-runtime: Pulling now. CLI output:
```
$ rwictl pool describe acme-enterprise-pool-1 --format json
{
  "id": "acme-enterprise-pool-1",
  "capacity_gpus": 64,
  "allocated_gpus": 63,
  "tenants": [{"name":"acme-enterprise","gpus":59,"priority":"pinned"},{"name":"batch-analytics","gpus":4,"priority":"best-effort"}],
  "autoscaler_state": "saturated",
  "burst_allowed": true
}
```

alice-ops: Observed spike from acme this morning correlated with a big batch reindex job. They have pinning enabled so autoscaler won't evict them automatically. Options: 1) ask acme to throttle, 2) evict/terminate best-effort tenants, 3) request short burst (if enterprise contract allows).

carol-customer-success: I'm on with the account exec. Need exact impact statement for the customer: are their latency timeouts occurring? Any 5xx? I can draft a message once we confirm mitigation path.

oncall-sre: Quick checks: 5xx rate for acme routes up 0.9% -> 3.8% in last 10m. Tail latency p99 > 4s. We need a mitigation within 10–15m. Eviction of best-effort tenants looks fastest. @eva-eng-sre can you confirm safe eviction steps?

eva-eng-sre: Confirmed. Plan: evict batch-analytics pods, drain two nodes reserved for best-effort, and trigger a short burst while we monitor. Eviction commands below (will run with --grace-period 30):
```bash
kubectl cordon node-xxx-be && kubectl drain node-xxx-be --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
# pod eviction: kubectl delete pod -n infra batch-analytics-*-* --force --grace-period=30
```
This will free ~6 GPUs. I'll coordinate with infra to avoid OOMs.

ben-eng-runtime: Note: autoscaler reports 'saturated' because acme has tenant_pin=true. Burst will require product/PM approval per cost controls. If approved we can attach 16 GPUs from burst pool in ~4m. Estimated incremental cost for this hour: ~$1.2k (charged to acme per contract).

dmitri-pm: I authorize a controlled burst of up to 16 GPUs for 30 minutes to restore SLOs provided CS ok's customer notification and cost agreement. Proceed with evictions + burst. Keep me in the loop.

oncall-sre: Proceeding with evictions now. @eva-eng-sre please run eviction and I will trigger burst once we see freed GPUs. Carol, draft customer note and hold until we have confirmation of burst.

carol-customer-success: Draft to customer (short):
"Hi Acme team — we're seeing your dedicated pool nearing capacity which is impacting response times for live requests. We're taking immediate steps: freeing non-critical batch capacity and temporarily adding short-lived burst capacity to stabilize latency. We'll monitor and follow up with root cause and next steps. ETA for stabilization ~10–20m. --Carol (Redwood)"

jordan-support: I'll DM the ACM (customer contact) and post the above in the support ticket. I'll be on standby to share progress.

eva-eng-sre: Evictions executed: freed 6 GPUs (batch-analytics pods). Pool state now:
```
allocated_gpus: 57 / 64
tenants: acme-enterprise:57
queue_latency: dropping
```
Requesting burst attach now.

oncall-sre: Attaching burst 16 GPUs...
ben-eng-runtime: Burst attach complete in 180s. New capacity: 73 GPUs total (64 base + 9 burst available to tenant due to placement). Autoscaler reported allocation adjustments.

oncall-sre: Metrics update: 5xx down to 0.6%, p99 latency down to 1.2s. Queue length trending to normal. Monitoring for 15m.

carol-customer-success: Sent customer message and updated support ticket with incident note and ETA. Customer acknowledges and thanks for rapid action.

dmitri-pm: Good. Assign postmortem to Ben + Eva + Ops to investigate why the reindex was allowed without throttling and to propose policy: auto-rate-limit for pinned tenants on sustained spikes.

oncall-sre: Agreed. I'll keep this incident open for the 15m monitoring window and then move to postmortem workflow. Handoff: I'm on until 14:45 UTC, then hand to next oncall @eva-eng-sre if still open.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Started: 3615009876. Mitigation actions: evicted best-effort tenant, attached 16-GPU burst, customer notified. Severity downgraded to P2.

oncall-sre: 15m monitor complete. Metrics stable for 20m. Closing incident channel. Postmortem ticket created: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/PM-3615

jordan-support: Noted. Will follow up with customer tomorrow to recap and share postmortem summary. :white_check_mark:

dmitri-pm: Thx team. Please include recommended guardrails (quota alerts earlier, optional throttles, and clearer burst-cost auto-approval thresholds) in the postmortem.

oncall-sre: Closing thread and handing off to postmortem owners. If anything regresses reopen or @oncall-sre. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
